[h1]We're back at 90% OFF!
Yes, the sale is back on![/h1]

[h3]It's finally time for another sale. The 30 days have passed and we're going balls out with a 90% discount. This is our style, go big or go home. 
[/h3]
The game, to recap, was created in less than six months from the awesome image below to published on Steam. The gang behind making the image come to life were students doing their internship, which also brought them from being students to being published developers. 

[h2]The game is super simple[/h2]
Yes, that is what it is. That is also what makes it fun. Versus a friend is of course best, but it's highly enjoyable facing off the AI. The Mayhem Mode has quickly become a favorite when demoing the game, and to be all honest we understand why. 15 balls on the court, with one being subtracted when a basket is made. It's kind of like the nursery rhyme about five birds on a tree branch. 

[h2]$2.50 will not even get you a cup of coffee [/h2]
That is in most cases true, and with the two-fifty price, we're hoping that quite a few new gamers will pick up the game. The reason is not to keep the lights on in the studio, but as it's great that the former students, nowadays devs, game get into the hands of more people. That is the end goal, to entertain gamers all over the world. Even the guy from China who refunded the game during the last sale - although we evidently fell short of entertaining him. Sorry, that is on us. 

Feel free to try it out and refund if you don't think it's worth the $2,50.

[b][h1]LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball [/h1][/b]
[h2]When the interns started to work on the game, the only design brief was what you see below.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44247747/53dcb36a6a083da5176f1c0bad8d232981070ae5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Made in Less than 6 Months[/h2]
The game, as mentioned in previous posts, was developed by game dev students during their internship. From scratch to finish, with only the image above and a verbal pitch to use for guidance. Naturally, along the way, there's been feedback, but the project was all hinging on the students being able to pull it off. Creating a game from scratch to release. They did, and they are all now published game developers. 

[h2]Simple Fun[/h2]
LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball is the simplest basketball game you will find, and that also makes it one of the games that anyone can play no matter how much or little gaming experience they have. 

[h2]Fun with Anyone[/h2]
Play against your partner, your parents, and your friends either locally or via Steam Remote Play Together. You'll have fun playing the nowadays celebrity AI, but you'll have the most fun playing against the earlier-mentioned group of people. 

[h2]Ambidextrous Play[/h2]
If you are ambidextrous, then you can even play against yourself in versus on the keyboard or on pads. You'll always walk away a winner - the other hands' defeat you can always sweep under the rug. 

[h2]Mayhem Mode[/h2]
We decided we also wanted to have an even more arcade type of gameplay, and we came up with more balls on the court - at the same time! Once a basket is made, the ball disappears and the player with the most baskets wins.

notes.title: About LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44247747/c55cf14149e76af948c4b375fb5e99efae323cd0.png[/img]

[h1]Less is More: A Northern Game Studio's Serendipitous Journey
[/h1]

In the realm of game development, chance encounters can lead to extraordinary ventures. Such is the case with Less is More, a new studio in Boden that emerged from an unexpected twist of fate. It all began with a simple inquiry about internship opportunities at a Stockholm-based studio. Little did anyone know that this query would lead to the birth of a fresh game dev studio up north close to the Arctic Circle.

With hardly any time to spare, the idea of Less is More was presented in a classroom in Boden. The vision was ambitious yet straightforward – create small games that could be developed during an internship period, transforming participating students into skilled game developers rather than mere students.

Traditionally, interns are often relegated to minor roles within massive projects, toiling away on a small cog in a vast machinery. At Less is More, however, every student is a vital cog in a finely tuned mechanism.

The impromptu presentation struck a chord and demanded an encore the following day when another class clamored to hear about the plans. It was then up to the students to express their interest and passion for the venture.

[h2]A Journey with 10 Bright Minds
[/h2]The studio's hope was for 2-3 passionate souls to join the endeavor, each bringing unique skills to the table. Initially, 11 individuals expressed interest, but one later stepped back, leaving an enthusiastic team of 10 students. With such talented minds, developing just one game wouldn't suffice. The decision was swiftly made to embark on two game projects.

The first game, reminiscent of the classic Pong, revolved around basketball. The second featured a side-scrolling racing game where players controlled a ball. Both projects had their own distinct ideas while sharing a common theme of physics centered around the ball.

[h2]The Power of Dynamic Presentations
[/h2]The student team was presented with straightforward concepts through sketches on a whiteboard. Even though the drawings resembled a child's handiwork, they perfectly aligned with the studio's philosophy of simplicity. Guided by these basic outlines, the students were given the freedom to solve challenges in their own way. Whenever they encountered roadblocks, seasoned developers were available to provide guidance and support.

The students eagerly set up shop in the studio and began crafting the two games. Divided into two teams, they seamlessly moved between projects, gaining invaluable experience in both. This hands-on approach would undoubtedly earn them a well-deserved spot in the credits.

[h2]LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball: A Futuristic Slam Dunk[/h2]
The basketball game, initially set to be the first to launch, was aptly named LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball. It perfectly encapsulated the essence of the game, a futuristic one-on-one basketball match. The title's inclusion of LiM (Less is More) might seem audacious, but as Disney has proven, ambitious ventures can yield remarkable results.

[h2]July 27, 2023 – Launching Towards Success[/h2]
Although the basketball game was completed in June, the team exercised caution and polished it further. Launching during Steam's major sale was avoided, as it might have overshadowed their hard work. Instead, the game debuted on July 27, providing ample time for planning exciting activities.

The second game, still nameless, is currently in development. More details will be unveiled in August if all proceeds according to plan.

[h2]A Triumph of Goals[/h2]
Less is More had a clear and resolute objective: release the games before the students' internship period ended, empowering them with a valuable addition to their resumes. They could proudly claim the title of published game developers, no longer mere game development students.

[h2]An Adventure of Growth[/h2]
Throughout this journey, the students learned invaluable lessons in teamwork, responsibility, and tenacity. They crossed the finish line, armed with newfound skills and fond memories.

[h1]You, the Player[/h1]
We invite you to [b]wishlist[/b] our game and await the first sale. Rest assured, it will be a 90% OFF sale, for we won't engage in a race to the bottom. At Less is More, we start at the bottom and stand our ground...

Thanks for reading.

notes.title: LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball is out today!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44247747/2194718975c6c09cbc1e2990a272b433fd6310f0.png[/img]

[h1][b]LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball is out today!
DON'T BUY IT!!![/b][/h1] 

[i]Now that sounds a bit weird.
Let us explain.[/i]

We have chosen to sell the game for the whopping sum of $49.99. That is WAAAAAAY too much for what the game should cost. Half of the profits go to charity and the rest to keep the lights on at the studio. But, and here's the but. As often as we can we will have the game on sale with 90% off, and that brings it down to $5. 

This is when you should buy the game if you're not interested in donating to charity. So wishlist today, and pick it up in 30 days or less.

For us as a studio and the chosen charity, it's better if you buy it at full price. [i]But we expect you to consider it when it's on discount - we would[/i]. If you're a Bitcoin billionaire, then, by all means, get it at full price. But if you're not, then simply wait for the next sale. 

[b]ABOUT LiM Beyond One-on-One Basketball[/b]
This is a game that was developed by students in the most northern gaming school in the world - or so we think. Research just takes time... 

A total of 10 students worked on two games like it was an extended Game Jam. On the first day, everything started from scratch with two ideas on two printer papers with hand written designs. And a little shy of six months later the game was done and ready for release. 

This also meant that today, all 10 students are not students anymore. They are published game developers! [b]Congratulations! [/b]

They are still students of life, but so are we all. The only conclusion we've arrived at so far in studying life is that it's better to have fun than not. And the more fun the better. Making tiny games is fun, releasing them is fun, and even telling you guys not to buy the game right now is also fun.

[b]To the players...[/b]
Remember that it's 10 new devs behind the game. You are most welcome to review the game fairly - you should, you always should. But feel very free to not be one of those guys who goes that extra mile to be offensive towards the devs. Thank you, and enjoy the game (in 30 days or less).

Less is More
